title: Consolidate to a single shared host age key bootstrapped via YubiKey
description:
Today each machine has its own age keypair (desktop, work-laptop, work-tmp) listed as a SOPS/git-agecrypt recipient. Adding a machine means generating a key, editing .sops.yaml and git-agecrypt.toml, and re-encrypting everything.

Replace this with one shared host age key whose private material is stored in the repo, encrypted with SOPS to the YubiKey recipient only. Provisioning a new machine then becomes: insert the YubiKey once, run a bootstrap recipe that decrypts the shared host key into ~/.config/sops/age/keys.txt and /var/lib/sops-nix/keys.txt, after which all SOPS secrets and git-agecrypt files decrypt without the YubiKey.
notes:
Implemented, verified, not yet committed.

Shared host key: age16fr85m3cp4g92mpyrzl6p3lldqzqlfc5nnkxn9tv6qaszjhrj3dqusgece

Verified on work-laptop: sops/home/secrets.yaml, sops/bootstrap/host-key.yaml and both private/** blobs all decrypt with the shared key alone. nix flake check passes, home-manager activation package and the work-laptop NixOS toplevel both evaluate/build.

Two follow-ups for the operator:

1. Commit promptly. The re-encrypted private/** blobs were written straight into the index with git update-index, bypassing the clean filter. Until they are in HEAD, any git add on those paths runs the clean filter, which reuses the ciphertext in HEAD and silently restores the old recipients.

2. /var/lib/sops-nix/keys.txt on work-laptop still holds the previous key; installing it needs sudo. Nothing under modules/sops declares secrets today, so nothing breaks, but running just bootstrap-host-key will bring it in line.

Old history of private/** stays readable with the YubiKey, which is still a recipient of those older blobs. ~/.config/sops/age/keys.txt.pre-shared-host-key.bak holds the previous work-tmp key as a convenience for reading old commits; it can be deleted once that is no longer wanted.
close_reason: Implemented and committed as 52b731a. Verified on work-laptop: sops/**, sops/bootstrap/host-key.yaml and both private/** blobs decrypt with the shared host key alone; nix flake check passes; home-manager activation package and the work-laptop NixOS toplevel build. just bootstrap runs end to end. Remaining machines (desktop, x13-laptop) each need just bootstrap-host-key once with the YubiKey.

title: Migrate low-sensitivity private data from git-crypt to git-agecrypt
description:
The repo currently uses two encryption systems with disjoint key material: SOPS (age keys, listed in .sops.yaml) for real secrets under sops/, and git-crypt (symmetric GPG-backed key) for low-sensitivity private data under secrets/ (SSH host addresses, AWS SSO config). The git-crypt key is separate key material that must be provisioned independently on every machine.

Migrate the git-crypt tree to git-agecrypt so both encryption systems share the same age recipients and identities. Also rename the directory and the Nix attribute from 'secrets' to 'private', since the contents are not secrets: they are private information that is acceptable to expose in the world-readable Nix store, unlike the SOPS-managed material.

Scope:
- secrets/ -> private/ (secrets.json -> hosts.json)
- .gitattributes: git-crypt filter -> git-agecrypt filter
- git-agecrypt.toml: recipients matching the age recipients in .sops.yaml
- Nix attribute 'secrets' -> 'private' in flake.nix, lib/mkHomeConfiguration.nix, lib/mkNixosConfiguration.nix, workstation/ssh.nix, workstation/home.nix
- Add git-agecrypt to home packages and document the per-checkout bootstrap
- Update AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md
notes:
Migration done and staged, not committed (global instruction: no commit without explicit user request).

Verified: staged blobs are age ciphertext, worktree plaintext intact, clean/smudge roundtrip works, nix build of homeConfigurations.oskar@x86_64-linux succeeds with resolved SSH HostNames and .aws/config, nix flake check --impure passes.

Follow-up worth noting: git history before this change still contains git-crypt-encrypted blobs, so the git-crypt symmetric key stays relevant for reading old commits. git-crypt is kept in home.packages for that reason. Removing it entirely would require a history rewrite.
close_reason: Migration complete: private/ encrypted with git-agecrypt using the same age recipients as .sops.yaml; nix build and nix flake check pass.

title: Migrate version-pinned sources to nvfetcher
description: Move version-pinned/manual-hash fetches (calibre-open-with, caveman-shrink, chrome-devtools-mcp, code-review-graph) and the two version-pinned emacs flake inputs (pgmacs, lsp-ltex-plus) to nvfetcher. Expose via pkgs.nvSources overlay; add just update-sources recipe; remove redundant flake inputs. HEAD-tracked emacs pkgs (claude-code-ide, gptel-quick, consult-mu) excluded - no upstream releases.
close_reason: nvfetcher migration complete; build + flake check green

title: Migrate code-review-graph from programs.claude-code.mcpServers (old) to programs.mcp.servers (new)
description:
code-review-graph.nix:71 is the last consumer of programs.claude-code.mcpServers after commit e09499f unified MCP config via programs.mcp.servers. Migration was missed because the file is commented out in default.nix:57.

Goal: move the mcpServers entry to programs.mcp.servers."code-review-graph" so opencode also picks it up. Coordinates with the agents.tools refactor (this entry becomes agents.tools.codeReviewGraph.mcpServers."code-review-graph").
acceptance_criteria: No references to programs.claude-code.mcpServers in workstation/agents/. code-review-graph appears in programs.mcp.servers when enable=true.

title: Refactor: mkMcpServer helper + extract package builds to packages/
description:
mcp-servers.nix has 7 server entries built 7 slightly-different ways. github-mcp and kagi hand-roll shell wrappers to inject sops secrets. caveman-shrink is wrapped inline at 5 callsites. kagimcp's 25-line Python build sits inside the registration file.

Goal: introduce mkMcpServer { name, command, args ? [], secretEnvFiles ? {}, shrink ? false } and mkEmacsStdioServer { name, initFunction, stopFunction }. Move kagimcp build to packages/kagimcp.nix; move chrome-devtools-mcp build (currently default.nix:11-28) to packages/chrome-devtools-mcp.nix. mcp-servers.nix becomes a registration file.
acceptance_criteria: No inline shell-script wrappers in mcp-servers.nix. No inline package builds. All 7 servers go through helper. github-mcp + kagi still receive their sops secrets. caveman-shrink wrapping preserved for the 5 currently-shrunk servers.

title: Refactor: rename agents docs to {both,claudeOnly,opencodeOnly} + fix AGENTS.md union
description:
Current naming is misleading: extraClaudeDocs means 'both', extraOpencodeDocs means 'opencode-only', extraClaudeOnlyDocs means 'claude-only'. Worse, ~/.agents/AGENTS.md (combined) excludes extraOpencodeDocs despite naming.

Goal: rename top-level options to agents.docs.{both, claudeOnly, opencodeOnly} (lists). Tool submodule's docs field appends to these. AGENTS.md becomes a true union (both + claudeOnly + opencodeOnly). claude-code context = both + claudeOnly. opencode context = both + opencodeOnly.

Touches: default.nix (options + fold), caveman.nix (extraOpencodeDocs -> docs.opencodeOnly), beads.nix (same), rtk.nix (extraClaudeDocs -> docs.both), subagents.nix (folded into default.nix per Candidate A).
acceptance_criteria: No references to extraClaudeDocs/extraOpencodeDocs/extraClaudeOnlyDocs in agents/. ~/.agents/AGENTS.md contains content from all three streams.

title: Refactor: introduce agents.tools.<name> submodule + central fold
description:
Workstation/agents/ tool integrations (caveman, rtk, beads, code-review-graph) lack a shared shape. code-review-graph is enabled by uncommenting default.nix:57; no module gates on enable; chrome-devtools-mcp build sits in default.nix while its registration is in mcp-servers.nix.

Goal: introduce typed submodule agents.tools.<name> with fields { enable (default true), packages, mcpServers, hooks, docs.{both,claudeOnly,opencodeOnly}, skills, activation }. default.nix filters by enable and folds active tools into programs.{claude-code,opencode,mcp}, home.packages, agents.extraSkillPaths, home.activation.

Edge cases (caveman hooksDir/statusLine, security-guidance enabledPlugins) bypass via direct programs.claude-code.settings.* gated on cfg.enable.

Pass-throughs (security-guidance.nix, subagents.nix) collapse into default.nix as inline declarations.
acceptance_criteria: agents.tools.caveman.enable = false; disables caveman entirely (no hooks, no docs, no packages). nix flake check passes. home-manager build evaluates. claude-code starts with all tools active when defaults preserved.

title: Migrate agent config to programs.claude-code / programs.opencode module options
description: Replace home.file/xdg.configFile writes in workstation/agents/{default,skills,caveman}.nix with typed module options (context, skills, hooksDir, settings). Enable programs.opencode. Verify with nix build .#packages.x86_64-linux.default.

value: nvfetcher manages version-pinned external sources (nvfetcher.toml -> _sources/generated.nix), exposed as the pkgs.nvSources overlay in lib/mkHomeConfiguration.nix and lib/mkNixosConfiguration.nix. Update with 'just update-sources' (nodejs on PATH for npm src.cmd entries). Covers: calibre-open-with, caveman-shrink, chrome-devtools-mcp, code-review-graph, pgmacs, lsp-ltex-plus. Decision: nvfetcher for release/version-pinned sources; HEAD-tracked emacs packages (claude-code-ide, gptel-quick, consult-mu) stay flake inputs because their upstreams publish no usable GitHub releases. Caveat: for npm packages nvfetcher only hashes the source tarball; buildNpmPackage's npmDepsHash (and chrome-devtools-mcp-lock.json) must still be regenerated by hand on a version bump.
